svg.text: 8 of 84 nodes are too small to label here; each names itself and its count on hover, and its colour is in the key above. Therapies are grouped into LINES
before being sequenced, by the definition every line count here shares: systemic-therapy treatment records (class, from SUBTYPE or else
TREATMENT_TYPE, on the systemic list: chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted, hormone, biologic, investigational and their spellings; radiation, surgery,
bone and ancillary treatment are not lines). A record starting more than 90 days after every earlier one has stopped begins a new line; anything closer is the
same line, and a line is labelled by its whole combination (sorted, so 'A + B' and 'B + A' are one regimen). That grouping is the point — a patient here has a
median of 6 treatment records and 4 distinct agents, and combination therapy is several records describing ONE decision, not several lines. Lines are
labelled by SUBTYPE. ENDING A PATH IS SPLIT IN TWO, because the difference matters more than anything else here: 'no further line' means the study kept
watching for at least 90 days (one line gap, the same rule that defines a line) and saw no further therapy; 'record ends here' means it did not, so nothing can
be concluded about that patient. 55.5% of paths end censored — reading those as patients who finished treatment would be a claim about the
record-keeping dressed up as one about the patient. Neither terminal is an outcome measure. 51 less common regimens folded into 'other', which is 23.3%
of first-line patients in the first panel — combination regimens have a genuinely long tail, so 'other' is real diversity rather than a rounding bucket. Raise topN
to split it further. Both panels share one scale and one colour per regimen, so their heights are directly comparable. TP53 mut: 11,564 with a first line; TP53
